problems.title: Graceful spider forests
problems.words: Spiders are trees with one central branching vertex. Show forests of spiders have the distinct-difference labeling.
problems.math: For any forest of spiders with $m$ edges and $c$ components, find a bijection $V\to\{0,\dots,m+c-1\}$ with distinct edge differences.

problems.title: Narrowing doorway sofa
problems.words: A width-1 hallway turns a right angle and then narrows to width 0.8. Find the biggest sofa that gets through.
problems.math: Maximize the area of a connected planar set movable from arm $\mathbb{R}_{<0}\times[0,1]$ into arm $[0,0.8]\times\mathbb{R}_{>1}$.

problems.title: Aperiodic polykite census
problems.words: The "hat" is made of 8 kites and tiles the plane only non-periodically. Find every such shape made of at most 12 kites.
problems.math: Enumerate all polykites with $\le12$ kites (from the $\{6,3\}$ kite grid) that tile $\mathbb{R}^2$ but admit no periodic tiling.

problems.title: Real-rank hyperoperations
problems.words: Addition, multiplication and exponentiation are ranks 1, 2, 3 of one ladder. Find natural rules that fix a unique operation at every real rank in between.
problems.math: Find axioms (analytic in $s$, $a[s{+}1](b{+}1)=a[s](a[s{+}1]b)$, agreement with $+,\times,\uparrow$ at $s=1,2,3$) that determine $a[s]b$ uniquely for real $s\in[1,3]$, and prove uniqueness.

problems.title: Hyperbolic sofa, flat limit
problems.words: As curvature fades to zero, the best hyperbolic sofa should approach Gerver's sofa. Find how fast.
problems.math: Let $A(\kappa)$ be the optimal sofa area in curvature $-\kappa$. Prove $A(\kappa)=2.2195\ldots+c\kappa+o(\kappa)$ and compute $c$.

problems.title: Formalize 3D Kakeya
problems.words: Turn the 2025 proof of the three-dimensional Kakeya conjecture into a compact computer-checked proof.
problems.math: Produce a Lean 4 formalization of the Wang–Zahl theorem ($\dim_H K=3$ for Kakeya $K\subset\mathbb{R}^3$) in under 50,000 lines beyond Mathlib.

problems.title: Hat patch complexity
problems.words: Count the distinct round patches of radius r in hat tilings. Find the exact constant in their growth.
problems.math: Let $P(r)$ count radius-$r$ patches over the hat tiling hull. Prove $P(r)\sim C r^2$ and compute $C$.

problems.title: Keller maps with few terms
problems.words: Find a Jacobian-conjecture counterexample using as few polynomial terms as possible.
problems.math: Minimize the total number of monomials of $F:\mathbb{C}^3\to\mathbb{C}^3$ with $\det DF\in\mathbb{C}^\times$ and $F$ not injective; prove minimality.

problems.title: The 2048 ceiling
problems.words: Show that even perfect play almost never reaches the theoretical top tile in 2048.
problems.math: Prove $\Pr(\text{reach }131072)<10^{-6}$ for every strategy on the $4\times4$ board with standard random spawns.

problems.title: Polyhedral sofa
problems.words: The best 3D sofa is curved. What is the best one with at most 12 flat corners?
problems.math: Maximize volume over convex polyhedra with $\le12$ vertices admissible in the $1\times1$ square corridor.

problems.title: FLT, compressed
problems.words: Fermat's Last Theorem has a huge computer formalization effort. Do it in far fewer lines.
problems.math: Give a Lean 4 proof of $x^n+y^n=z^n\Rightarrow xyz=0$ for $n\ge3$ using at most $10^5$ lines beyond current Mathlib.

problems.title: Blokus Duo
problems.words: Who wins two-player Blokus with perfect play?
problems.math: Weakly solve Blokus Duo on the $14\times14$ board with standard starting points.

problems.title: Go on a torus
problems.words: Go on a 7 × 7 board that wraps around. What komi makes the game fair?
problems.math: Determine the perfect-play score of Go on $\mathbb{Z}_7^2$ (area scoring, positional superko).

problems.title: Random graceful forests
problems.words: Almost every random forest has the distinct-edge-difference labeling.
problems.math: For a uniform random forest with $m$ edges and $c\sim\alpha m$ components, prove the graceful-forest labeling exists with probability $\to1$.

problems.title: T-junction sofa
problems.words: A sofa comes up the stem of a T and must be able to leave by either arm. Find the biggest one.
problems.math: Maximize area over sets admissible from the stem to each arm (separately) of a width-1 T-junction.

problems.title: Hat billiard counting
problems.words: Count the periodic bouncing paths inside a hat-shaped table up to a given length.
problems.math: For billiards in the hat polygon, prove $N(L)\sim cL^2$ for periodic cylinder families and compute $c$.

problems.title: Fast Prime Nim
problems.words: Compute Prime Nim values up to a trillion.
problems.math: Give an algorithm computing $G(n)$ for all $n\le10^{12}$ in time $o(N^{1.5})$ and run it.

problems.title: Emirps, almost
problems.words: Show infinitely many primes have a reversal with at most three prime factors.
problems.math: Prove $\#\{p\le x: \Omega(\operatorname{rev}(p))\le3\}\to\infty$.

problems.title: Smallest-factor Collatz, almost always
problems.words: For the smallest-odd-factor Collatz map, almost every start reaches 1.
problems.math: Prove $g^k(n)=1$ for some $k$, for a density-1 set of $n$.

problems.title: Leaky firefighting
problems.words: Fire spreads to each neighbour only with probability p. Find the largest p at which one firefighter per turn wins.
problems.math: On $\mathbb{Z}^2$ with each burning–unburnt edge transmitting independently with probability $p$, find $p^*$ such that one protection per turn contains the fire a.s. iff $p<p^*$.

problems.title: Small Hadwiger counterexample
problems.words: The claimed counterexamples to Hadwiger's conjecture are astronomically large. Find one under a million vertices.
problems.math: Find $G$ with $|V(G)|<10^6$ and $h(G)<\chi(G)$, or prove every counterexample is larger.

problems.title: Unbounded Prime Nim
problems.words: Do the Prime Nim values grow without limit?
problems.math: Decide whether $\sup_n G(n)=\infty$ for the prime subtraction game.

problems.title: Ringel for forests
problems.words: Split a complete graph on 2m + 1 vertices into identical copies of any given forest with m edges.
problems.math: Prove $K_{2m+1}$ decomposes into $2m+1$ copies of any forest with $m$ edges.

problems.title: Geodesic squares on surfaces
problems.words: Every smooth closed curve on a convex surface should pass through the corners of a square made of shortest paths.
problems.math: Prove every smooth simple closed curve on a smooth convex surface inscribes a geodesic quadrilateral with equal sides and equal diagonals.

problems.title: Prime Nim is not automatic
problems.words: No finite machine reading digits can recognize Prime Nim losing positions.
problems.math: Prove the P-position set is not $k$-automatic for any base $k\ge2$.

problems.title: Integer-bijective Keller map
problems.words: Find a polynomial map with Jacobian 1 that shuffles integer points perfectly but has no polynomial inverse.
problems.math: Find $F\in\mathbb{Z}[x]^n$, $\det DF\equiv1$, inducing a bijection of $\mathbb{Z}^n$ but not a polynomial automorphism.

problems.title: Twin-free stretches
problems.words: Find long stretches full of primes but containing no twin primes.
problems.math: Prove there are intervals $[x,x+(\log x)^{1.1}]$ with $\ge(\log x)^{0.05}$ primes but no twin pair, for infinitely many $x$.

problems.title: Big factors of p² + p + 1
problems.words: For primes p, show p² + p + 1 often has a very large prime factor.
problems.math: Prove $P(p^2+p+1)>p^{1.5}$ for infinitely many primes $p$.

problems.title: Cops on square sums
problems.words: How many cops catch a robber moving along square-sum links?
problems.math: Determine $c(S_N)$, the cop number of the square-sum graph, for all large $N$.

problems.title: Random walks on square sums
problems.words: How long does a random walk on the square-sum graph take to forget its starting point?
problems.math: Determine the mixing time of simple random walk on the giant component of $S_N$ up to constants.

problems.title: Sudoku completions are log-normal
problems.words: Erase half a random Sudoku. The number of ways to refill it should follow a log-normal law.
problems.math: For a random $9\times9$ grid with a uniformly random half of cells erased, prove $\log(\#\text{completions})$ is asymptotically normal under the natural $n^2\times n^2$ scaling.

problems.title: Cube-sum colors
problems.words: Join numbers that add up to a perfect cube. Show a fixed number of colors always suffices.
problems.math: For $C_N$ with $a\sim b\iff a+b$ a cube, prove $\sup_N\chi(C_N)<\infty$ and find it.

problems.title: Lonely runner, bounded speeds
problems.words: Prove the lonely runner conjecture whenever all speeds are at most 10 times the number of runners.
problems.math: Prove $\sup_t\min_i\|tv_i\|\ge\frac1{n+1}$ for all distinct $v_i\le10n$.

problems.title: Wind-driven fire in 3D
problems.words: In 3D, fire spreads in five of six directions because of wind. How many firefighters per turn are needed?
problems.math: On $\mathbb{Z}^3$ with spread to all neighbours except $-e_1$, find the least per-turn budget containing a single fire.

problems.title: Keller maps of degree 4
problems.words: Show that every 3D polynomial map of degree at most 4 with constant Jacobian has a polynomial inverse.
problems.math: Prove $F:\mathbb{C}^3\to\mathbb{C}^3$, $\deg F\le4$, $\det DF\in\mathbb{C}^\times$ implies $F$ is an automorphism.

problems.title: Hyperbolic lonely runners
problems.words: Runners move along closed paths on a hyperbolic surface. Show one eventually gets far from all others.
problems.math: For geodesic flows on a closed hyperbolic surface along $n$ distinct primitive closed geodesics, prove a uniform separation time exists, with optimal bound.

problems.title: Fire spotting threshold
problems.words: Embers jump ahead of a fire. Find the jump probability where firefighting becomes hopeless.
problems.math: On $\mathbb{Z}^2$, a burning cell also ignites a uniformly random cell at distance $\le r$ with probability $q$. Find $q^*(r,k)$ beyond which $k$ protections per turn fail a.s.

problems.title: Smoke-free corridor
problems.words: Show a corridor's smoke clears in a predictable time when air flows through it.
problems.math: For advection–diffusion in a periodic corridor with Stokes flow, find the sharp exponential decay rate of a passive scalar in terms of geometry.

problems.title: Wythoff Prime Nim
problems.words: With two piles, remove a prime from one pile or the same prime from both. Describe the losing positions.
problems.math: Characterize the P-positions of the two-pile game with moves $(a,b)\to(a-p,b),(a,b-p),(a-p,b-p)$, $p$ prime.

problems.title: Polykite growth constant
problems.words: Count shapes made of n kites. Find the exponential growth rate to three digits.
problems.math: Let $k_n$ count polykites with $n$ kites up to congruence. Prove $k_n^{1/n}\to\lambda$ and compute $\lambda$ to 3 digits.

problems.title: Odd-cycle-free square sums
problems.words: How many numbers up to N can you keep so the square-sum graph on them has no odd cycle?
problems.math: Determine $\max\{|A|:A\subseteq[N],\ S_N[A]\text{ bipartite}\}/N$ asymptotically.

problems.title: Hot spots on the hat
problems.words: Heat a hat-shaped insulated plate. Decide whether the hottest point eventually sits on the boundary.
problems.math: Decide whether a second Neumann eigenfunction of the hat polygon attains its maximum only on $\partial\Omega$.

problems.title: The angel on the hat
problems.words: An angel moves up to k tiles per turn on a hat tiling; a devil deletes one tile per turn. Find the least k for which the angel escapes forever.
problems.math: Determine the least $k$ such that the angel of power $k$ (moves to any tile within graph distance $k$) wins against the devil on every hat tiling's adjacency graph.

problems.title: Square-sum paths with chosen ends
problems.words: Show you can line up 1 to N with neighbours summing to squares, starting and ending at almost any two numbers you choose.
problems.math: Prove $S_N$ contains a Hamiltonian path whose endpoints can be prescribed arbitrarily among vertices of degree $\ge3$, for all large $N$.

problems.title: Isoperimetric profile of the spectre
problems.words: Among all clusters of n spectre tiles, find the smallest possible perimeter, asymptotically, with the exact constant.
problems.math: Prove $\min\{|\partial S|:S$ a union of $n$ tiles in a spectre tiling$\}\sim c\sqrt n$ and determine $c$.

problems.title: Kissing numbers of polykite families
problems.words: Show the hat's family of shapes has a kissing number that jumps at exactly one parameter value.
problems.math: For Tile$(a,b)$, $a,b>0$, let $k(a,b)$ be the kissing number (congruent copies, reflections allowed). Prove $k$ is piecewise constant with finitely many jumps and find them.

problems.title: Graceful forests from caterpillar seeds
problems.words: Show forests made of large caterpillars plus one arbitrary tree are graceful-forest labelable.
problems.math: Prove every forest $T\cup C_1\cup\dots\cup C_k$ with $T$ any tree and $C_i$ caterpillars each of size $\ge|T|$ admits a bijection $V\to\{0,\dots,m+k\}$ with distinct edge differences.

problems.title: Chromatic number of prime-difference plus square-sum
problems.words: Join two numbers if their sum is a square or their difference is prime. Find the colours needed for all positive integers.
problems.math: Determine $\chi(G)$ for $G$ on $\mathbb{N}$ with $a\sim b$ iff $a+b$ is a square or $|a-b|$ is prime.

problems.title: The hat is not spectral
problems.words: Fuglede's conjecture predicts that a shape that cannot tile by translations has no orthogonal basis of exponentials. Prove this for the hat.
problems.math: Prove there is no $\Lambda\subset\mathbb{R}^2$ with $\{e^{2\pi i\lambda\cdot x}\}_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ an orthogonal basis of $L^2(\text{hat})$.

problems.title: Prime-sum Hamiltonian cycles through every edge
problems.words: Show every edge of the prime-sum graph on 1 to 2n lies on a full prime circle.
problems.math: Prove for all large $n$ every edge of the prime-sum graph on $[2n]$ lies on a Hamiltonian cycle.

problems.title: Polykite growth: one more digit
problems.words: Pin the exponential growth rate of n-kite shapes to within one percent, rigorously.
problems.math: Prove explicit bounds $a\le\lambda\le b$ with $b/a\le1.01$ for the polykite growth constant $\lambda=\lim k_n^{1/n}$.

problems.title: Long loops for affine prime maps
problems.words: As a and b vary, the loops of p ↦ largest prime factor of ap + b get longer and longer. Prove loop lengths are unbounded.
problems.math: Prove $\sup_{a,b}\max\{\text{length of a cycle of } p\mapsto P(ap+b)\}=\infty$.

problems.title: High-dimensional sofa
problems.words: How does the best sofa's volume grow in an n-dimensional corridor?
problems.math: Determine the asymptotics in $n$ of the optimal volume in the $n$-dimensional right-angled corridor of unit cross-section.

problems.title: Polykite structure theorem
problems.words: Classify every shape of up to 20 kites: tiles periodically, tiles only aperiodically, or fails within a few layers.
problems.math: Prove each polykite with $\le20$ kites either tiles periodically, tiles only aperiodically, or has Heesch number $\le10$.

problems.title: Sparse Keller maps
problems.words: List every Jacobian-conjecture counterexample in 3D built from at most 12 monomials in total, up to symmetry.
problems.math: Classify all non-invertible Keller maps $\mathbb{C}^3\to\mathbb{C}^3$ whose three components together have at most 12 monomials, up to affine changes of coordinates.

problems.title: Time-independent force
problems.words: Make viscous fluid blow up with a push that never changes in time.
problems.math: Construct smooth compactly supported time-independent $f$ such that 3D Navier–Stokes from rest blows up in finite time.

problems.title: Square-sum pancyclicity
problems.words: Show the square-sum graph has cycles of every possible length.
problems.math: Prove $S_N$ is pancyclic on its 2-connected core for all large $N$.

problems.title: Gomoku on hats
problems.words: Prove the first player wins five-in-a-row on an infinite board of hat tiles.
problems.math: Prove the first player has a winning strategy in the 5-in-a-row game on the hat adjacency graph (rows = geodesic paths).

problems.title: Vorticity growth in a hat
problems.words: Fluid in a hat-shaped container should develop sharper and sharper swirls near its corners.
problems.math: For 2D Euler in the hat polygon, prove $\|\nabla\omega(t)\|_\infty$ grows double exponentially for some smooth initial data.

problems.title: Fluid in a box blows up
problems.words: Show viscous fluid in a closed box with sticky walls can blow up under a smooth push.
problems.math: Construct smooth $f$ such that 3D Navier–Stokes with no-slip in the unit cube blows up in finite time.

problems.title: Cross-polytopes in 4D
problems.words: Every 4D convex body should have the corners of a regular cross-polytope on its boundary.
problems.math: Prove every convex body in $\mathbb{R}^4$ has an inscribed regular cross-polytope.

problems.title: Sofa with a rotating door
problems.words: A door at the corner swings shut as you move. Find the largest shape that still gets through.
problems.math: Determine the maximal area of a set passing the width-1 right-angled corridor while the region $\{x>1,y>1\}$ moves by a prescribed rotating half-line barrier.

problems.title: Fire on a random hat patch
problems.words: Remove each hat tile with some probability. Find the exact point where a fire can no longer burn forever.
problems.math: Prove the site-percolation threshold of the hat tiling exists as a single sharp value and bound it within $10^{-4}$.

problems.title: Seven-free Goldbach
problems.words: Show almost every even number is a sum of two primes that have no digit 7.
problems.math: Prove all but $o(x)$ even $n\le x$ are sums of two 7-free primes.

problems.title: Hyperdissipative forced blow-up
problems.words: Fluids with extra strong viscosity never blow up above a known threshold. Show forced blow-up still happens just below it.
problems.math: For $\partial_tu+(u\cdot\nabla)u+\nabla p=-(-\Delta)^{\alpha}u+f$ on $\mathbb{R}^3$, construct smooth compactly supported $f$ giving finite-time blow-up from rest for every $\alpha<5/4$.

problems.title: Unit distances in three dimensions after 2026
problems.words: The 2026 number-field idea beat Erdős in the plane. Adapt it to unit distances among points on a sphere in 3D.
problems.math: Prove there are $n$-point sets on the unit sphere $S^2$ with $\ge n^{1+c}$ pairs at distance $1$, for some $c>0$ and infinitely many $n$.

problems.title: Seven-free Gaussian primes
problems.words: Show infinitely many primes a² + b² have both a and b free of the digit 7.
problems.math: Prove infinitely many primes $a^2+b^2$ with $a,b$ positive integers free of the decimal digit 7.

problems.title: Four-term square-sum chains in primes
problems.words: Find infinitely many chains of four primes where each neighbouring pair sums to a square.
problems.math: Prove infinitely many 4-tuples of primes $p_1,p_2,p_3,p_4$ with $p_i+p_{i+1}$ a square for $i=1,2,3$.

problems.title: Missing digits in two bases
problems.words: Show infinitely many primes have no digit 9 in base 10 and no digit 10 in base 11 at the same time.
problems.math: Prove infinitely many primes whose base-10 expansion avoids the digit 9 and whose base-11 expansion avoids the digit 10.

problems.title: Bombieri–Vinogradov for seven-free primes in base 10
problems.words: Show seven-free primes are well distributed in arithmetic progressions on average over moduli up to x^θ, for some θ > 0, in base 10.
problems.math: Prove there is $\theta>0$ such that $\sum_{q\le x^\theta}\max_{(a,q)=1}\big|\pi_7(x;q,a)-\frac{\pi_7(x)}{\varphi(q)}\big|\ll_A \pi_7(x)(\log x)^{-A}$, where $\pi_7$ counts 7-free primes (moduli coprime to 10).

problems.title: Three colors for cube sums
problems.words: Can the positive integers be 3-colored so no two numbers of the same color add to a cube? Settle it.
problems.math: Decide whether $\chi(C_\infty)\le3$, where $a\sim b$ iff $a+b$ is a perfect cube.

problems.title: Hat ground state
problems.words: Find the arrangement of hat tiles that minimises a natural energy, and show it is the aperiodic tiling.
problems.math: Prove the hat tiling is the unique (up to isometry) ground state of a finite-range two-body potential on hat-shaped particles in the plane.

problems.title: Delayed fire on the grid
problems.words: If the fire only spreads every other turn, find the smallest per-turn budget that always contains it.
problems.math: Find the infimum of average firefighter budgets that contain the half-speed fire on $\mathbb{Z}^2$.

problems.title: Packing hats
problems.words: Find the densest way to pack hat shapes when they are not allowed to tile.
problems.math: Determine the maximal packing density of translates and rotations of the hat with reflections forbidden.

problems.title: Hat corona limit shape is not polygonal
problems.words: Show the limiting shape of hat layers has a fractal outline.
problems.math: Prove the limit shape of scaled hat coronas has boundary of Hausdorff dimension $>1$.

problems.title: Prime Nim with prime-power moves
problems.words: Allow subtracting any prime power. Find exactly which piles lose.
problems.math: Characterize the P-positions of the subtraction game with move set $\{p^k: p\text{ prime},k\ge1\}$.

problems.title: Sofa through a revolving corridor
problems.words: The hallway itself slowly rotates while you push the sofa. Find the largest sofa that still makes it.
problems.math: For the width-1 L-corridor rotating at angular speed $\omega$ relative to a sofa moving at unit speed, find the optimal area as a function of $\omega$.

problems.title: Square-sum chains in primes
problems.words: Show there are arbitrarily long chains of primes where neighbours sum to squares.
problems.math: Prove for every $k$ there are primes $p_1,\dots,p_k$ with $p_i+p_{i+1}$ a perfect square for all $i<k$.

problems.title: Cube-sum independence
problems.words: Find the largest set of numbers up to N where no two add to a cube.
problems.math: Determine $\alpha(C_N)$ asymptotically, with second-order term.

problems.title: Hat Ising free energy
problems.words: Find the exact free energy of magnets on a hat tiling at the critical point.
problems.math: Compute $f(\beta_c)$ for the Ising model on the hat graph in closed form.

problems.title: Wind-driven fire
problems.words: On a grid, fire spreads each turn only east, north and south (the wind blocks westward spread). How few firefighters per turn can always trap a single burning cell?
problems.math: On $\mathbb{Z}^2$, burning cells ignite neighbours at offsets $(1,0),(0,\pm1)$ each turn; $k$ unburnt cells are protected per turn. Find the least $k$ that always yields a finite burned set.

problems.title: Lonely runner with one fast runner
problems.words: Runners have speeds 1, 2, 3 and some larger speed m. Work out exactly how lonely a stationary runner is guaranteed to get, depending on m.
problems.math: Compute $\delta(m)=\sup_t\min(\|t\|,\|2t\|,\|3t\|,\|mt\|)$ in closed form for all integers $m\ge4$.

problems.title: Smallest-odd-factor Collatz
problems.words: Halve even numbers; send an odd number to the smallest odd prime dividing 3n + 1. Find every cycle that occurs below a billion.
problems.math: Let $g(n)=n/2$ ($n$ even) and $g(n)=q(3n+1)$ ($n$ odd), $q$ the least odd prime factor ($1$ if none). Classify all cycles of $g$ meeting $[1,10^9]$.

problems.title: Anti-knight Sudoku
problems.words: In this Sudoku, equal digits may not sit a knight's move apart. What is the fewest clues for a unique solution?
problems.math: Determine the minimum number of givens in a uniquely solvable $9\times9$ Sudoku with the extra anti-knight constraint.

problems.title: Voice leading is NP-hard
problems.words: Moving n voices through a chord progression with the least total motion while avoiding parallel fifths should be computationally hard.
problems.math: Show NP-hardness of minimizing $\sum_t\sum_i |x_{t+1,i}-x_{t,i}|$ over voicings of a given chord sequence with $n$ voices, subject to no parallel perfect fifths.

problems.title: Two-tree graceful forests
problems.words: Check the distinct-difference labeling for every forest of two small trees.
problems.math: Prove that every forest of two trees with at most 25 vertices each has a bijection $V\to\{0,\dots,m+1\}$ with distinct edge differences.

problems.title: Kissing hats
problems.words: How many copies of the hat tile can touch one hat without overlapping?
problems.math: Determine the maximum number of interior-disjoint congruent copies of the hat polykite, reflections allowed, each meeting a fixed hat.

problems.title: Square in a snowflake
problems.words: Find the largest square whose four corners lie on the Koch snowflake.
problems.math: Prove the Koch snowflake inscribes a square, and determine the maximal side length of an inscribed square.

problems.title: Billiards in the sofa
problems.words: A ball bounces inside Gerver's sofa shape. Find its shortest closed bouncing path.
problems.math: Determine the minimal-length periodic billiard trajectory in Gerver's sofa and prove minimality.

problems.title: Fire on the Sierpinski graph
problems.words: With one firefighter per turn on the Sierpinski triangle graph, what fraction must burn as the graph gets bigger?
problems.math: On the level-$n$ Sierpinski gasket graph with a fire at a corner and one protected vertex per turn, find $\lim_n \min |B|/|V|$.

problems.title: Prime squared square
problems.words: Tile a square with smaller squares, all different sizes, every side a prime number. Find one or show none exists.
problems.math: Find a perfect squared square whose component squares all have prime side lengths, or prove none exists.

problems.title: Five colors for square sums
problems.words: Square-sum graphs need four colors eventually. Do they eventually need five?
problems.math: Decide whether $\chi(S_N)\ge5$ for all sufficiently large $N$.

problems.title: Coloring the spectre's distances
problems.words: Take all corners of a spectre tiling and join two whenever they are exactly one edge-length apart. How many colors are needed?
problems.math: Determine the chromatic number of the unit-distance graph on the vertex set of a spectre tiling (unit = edge length).

problems.title: Isospectral polykites
problems.words: Two different drums can sound the same. Find two different shapes made of kites that do.
problems.math: Find two non-congruent polykites whose Dirichlet Laplacians have identical spectra.

problems.title: Random lonely runners
problems.words: With random speeds, runners get noticeably lonelier than the conjecture promises.
problems.math: For i.i.d. uniform speeds in $[1,N]$, $N\gg n^3$, prove the loneliness gap exceeds $\frac1{n+1}+c\frac{\log n}{n^2}$ with probability $\to1$.

problems.title: BB(5), compressed
problems.words: The Busy Beaver value BB(5) was proved with a large computer proof. Make it small.
problems.math: Prove $BB(5)=47{,}176{,}870$ in Lean 4 in under 10,000 lines.

problems.title: Lean golf is hard to approximate
problems.words: Not only is the shortest basic-tactic proof hard to find; even a roughly short one is.
problems.math: Prove intro/apply/exact/rfl proof minimization admits no constant-factor approximation unless P = NP.

problems.title: Exotic shuffles
problems.words: For which deck sizes do the three-pile shuffles generate every possible arrangement?
problems.math: Determine all $n$ for which the six 3-pile shuffles generate $S_{3n}$ or $A_{3n}$.

problems.title: Hyperoperation Goodstein
problems.words: A Goodstein-style sequence using hyperoperations always ends, but ordinary arithmetic cannot prove it.
problems.math: Define base-change on hereditary hyperoperation normal forms; prove the sequences terminate and termination is unprovable in PA.

problems.title: One firefighter on hats
